$comment: Glossary entries (plan section 9). Each links a game concept to a real mission or dataset. VERIFY-marked entries need a source in docs/CREDITS.md before shipping.

entries.text: The gap between 'enough' and 'enough even when things go wrong'. Shapla-1 had none. Real missions keep 20-30% on power and mass.
Every orbit crosses Earth's shadow. A 500 km satellite spends about 35 minutes of each 95-minute orbit in the dark. VERIFY: eclipse fraction asin(Re/a)/pi.

Cameras that measure heat can see at night, and cyclone cloud-top temperature tells forecasters how strong the storm is. Real weather satellites always carry one. VERIFY: e.g. VIIRS on Suomi NPP/NOAA-20.
Radar that paints the ground with its own signal and listens for the echo. It sees through clouds and at night — and maps floods under the monsoon. VERIFY: e.g. NASA-ISRO NISAR, ESA Sentinel-1.
An orbit tilted so the satellite crosses every place at the same local solar time — same lighting every day, easy to compare images. VERIFY: typical 600-800 km, ~98° inclination.
The radio pipeline home. An S-band transmitter manages about 1 Mbps; X-band 10+. Pictures you cannot send home are pictures you never took.
